segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 49: More Drafts Than Can Be Used

The sight of Xu Youyu sighing on the sofa reminded Li Luo of the time in their past life when their relationship was at its best.

Back then, Xu Youyu's new book was gaining great momentum. She hadn't been selected as one of the year's Twelve Heavenly Kings yet, and her web novel career was just in its budding stage.

But it was also then that Xu Youyu, from pulling all-nighters every day to write ten thousand words and climb the charts, had a particularly rough period, her stomach cramping painfully in the middle of the night.

Li Luo received her call at three or four in the morning, got up in the dark and ran to her place, took her to the hospital for an IV drip, and then brought her back home to take her medicine and be cared for.

It was also during that time that Li Luo came over daily to cook for her, which was how Xu Youyu learned that he had such a skill.

So much so that even after she had clearly recovered, she pretended to still be unwell, mooching food and drinks all day, making Li Luo come and cook for her.

When Li Luo later found out, he didn't expose her, still coming over to cook every day. Eventually, he even started bringing his laptop to her place so they could write together.

Recalling these things, Li Luo returned to the present and looked at Xu Youyu on the sofa with a knowing smile.

"Mmm... it smells so good." Having just finished her shower, Ying Chanxi, now in a pair of panda pajamas and drying her hair with a towel, walked over from the hallway.

Li Luo pushed a small bowl of fried rice he had prepared to the front of the table and reached out to take the towel from her hands. "You sit, I'll dry it for you."

"Oh." Ying Chanxi glanced at Xu Youyu out of the corner of her eye, then pursed her lips and sat down. She cupped the bowl and chopsticks in her small hands, savoring the food in small bites while enjoying Li Luo's hair-drying service.

Xu Youyu, quite used to this scene, rolled over on the sofa, put on her slippers, and stretched. "Well, I'm heading back to my room. You two sleep early. Tomorrow's military training is going to be tough."

"Goodnight, Senior Sister~"

"Mhm, goodnight, Xixi."

"Senior Sister." Li Luo, holding the hairdryer, turned his head to look at Xu Youyu.

"Hmm? What's up?" Xu Youyu tilted her head, a puzzled look on her face.

"You haven't done the dishes yet."

Xu Youyu: "..."

Watching Xu Youyu sheepishly walk into the kitchen to do the dishes, Li Luo continued to dry Ying Chanxi's hair.

After he was done, Li Luo stretched and reminded Ying Chanxi to wash her own bowl and chopsticks before turning and heading back to his bedroom.

He opened his computer and took a look.

On Friday, *I'm Really Not a Star* went on sale, getting 1,800 first-day subscriptions. This result was within expectations.

By maintaining a daily update of four thousand words, he would definitely earn five to six thousand yuan a month in royalties, which at a minimum could offset the family's mortgage payments.

Reaching this stage had basically satisfied Li Luo's initial needs.

As for how far this book could go in the future, that was for time to tell.

With that in mind, Li Luo took another look at Xu Youyu's *Literary Era*.

This book had a little over 800 first-day subscriptions after going on sale, which would work out to more than three thousand yuan a month in royalties.

For a high school student, this was quite a large sum.

Even though Xu Youyu's family was well-off, after accounting for normal food and rent expenses, her family only gave her about five hundred yuan a month for pocket money.

Compared to the more than three thousand yuan in royalties, for a high school student, it wouldn't be an exaggeration to call it the high school version of financial freedom.

Li Luo thought back to his own high school days in his past life. If he had an extra three thousand yuan in pocket money each month, he couldn't imagine how suave and confident he would have been.

Thinking about it, Xu Youyu really was impressive, already earning money by writing web novels in high school.

Moreover, at such a young age, her writing style and prose were already quite refined, far beyond what a cliché-style writer like Li Luo could compare to.

For Li Luo, he was just applying the well-worn tropes from the web novel circles of the future, weaving stories according to various classic plot points. He simply stuffed a well-known work into every plotline to complete his content creation.

In comparison, the showbiz novel Li Luo wrote was a typical progression-focused story. As long as the author wanted, it could go on in an infinite loop.

Xu Youyu's *Literary Era*, on the other hand, was plot-driven. Although it had similar plot devices, it primarily served the story the author wanted to write.

Of course, the truly impressive ones were those who could perfectly integrate the progression-focused tropes into the overall plot framework.

A work like *Lord of the Mysteries*, which Li Luo loved in his later years, had reached that level.

As he thought about this, Li Luo had already set up scheduled posts for the next week's updates.

Looking at the full 250,000 words of drafted manuscripts in his drafts folder, Li Luo felt a great sense of security.

Even if he didn't write a single word from now on, these drafts were enough for him to coast on for two months.

Just then, as Li Luo was about to take a shower, he received a QQ message.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: Big shot, look!

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: [Image]

Li Luo glanced at it curiously, wondering what kind of picture Xu Youyu would send him in the middle of the night.

If it were his past life, Li Luo would guess it was probably some lewd picture.

But as the high school student Xu Youyu was now, she probably wouldn't be that outrageous.

After a closer look, it was just as he thought.

It was a screenshot of a word count, showing ten thousand words.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: My draft is already ten thousand words long. How about that, impressive, right?

If it were back when he was writing web novels in his past life, faced with a draft of over ten thousand words, Li Luo would have definitely praised her as amazing.

But now, reborn and armed with a 250,000-word draft, Li Luo could only chuckle and send a screenshot of his own.

Rekindle: Although a ten-thousand-word draft is impressive, I can only say you still need more practice.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: ???

Sitting at her computer in the study, Xu Youyu had been smugly awaiting Li Luo's exclamation of "holy crap."

But when she saw the twenty-five thousand-word draft that Li Luo sent, her eyes widened.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: How do you have such a big draft? Over twenty thousand words???

Rekindle: I suggest you count again, more carefully.

Huh?

Seeing this, Xu Youyu looked doubtfully at the screenshot he had sent. When she counted the digits in the word count, she was completely stunned for a moment.

Two... two hundred and fifty thousand words?

For real?

Xu Youyu sat dumbfounded in front of her computer, feeling as if her entire worldview had been shattered.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: Let's just block each other. I'm done talking.

Rekindle: Don't be discouraged, I've been saving up these words for a long time.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: How long?

Rekindle: Less than two months, I guess.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: Block! Block! Get lost!

Less than two months, wasn't that from the very beginning of the book until now?

She had just managed to write 250,000 words in total, while Li Luo had already finished 500,000.

Was he even giving others a chance to live?

Xu Youyu thought resentfully, and finally pounded on her keyboard to reply to him.

Sleep Early to Grow Taller: Just you wait! I'll surpass you sooner or later!

Li Luo definitely wouldn't be able to write during the next few days of military training. She had to use this time to catch up!

But just as she opened Word, ready to get to work, the image of a massive 250,000 words popped into her head, and her motivation instantly vanished.

Forget it.

Maybe this is just what talent looks like.

Thinking this, Xu Youyu got up, threw herself onto her bed, and fell asleep.

Running away might be shameful, but it sure was effective.

Meanwhile, after Ying Chanxi finished washing the dishes, she took out the military training uniform issued by the school and tried it on in her room.

A short while later, she knocked on Li Luo's door, looking somewhat distressed.

"What's wrong?" Li Luo opened the door and saw Ying Chanxi dressed in army green, asking strangely.

"Do you have a belt?" Ying Chanxi tugged at the loose waistband of her pants. "It seems like the training uniform I got didn't come with a belt."
